newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 14.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - S.Korean newspapers - Jan 14.

text.p: The following is a summary of major South Korean political stories in leading newspapers, prepared by Reuters in Seoul. Reuters has not checked the stories and does not guarantee their accuracy. Telephone: (822) 727-5650. Fax: (822) 727-5666.

- One senior government official said a three-nation briefing between North Korea, South Korea, and the United States is going to be held in New York on January 29 (NY time) in preparation for the four-party talks to be held later among North and South Korea, the United States, and China.

- As the Federation of Korean Trade Unions (FKTU) will join nationwide strikes on a limited basis on January 14 and 15, it is expected that this week will be a decisive point in unionists' demands for the nullification of new labour legislation. Concerns are also rising over difficulties forced upon the public as most of the public sector including subway workers will go on full strike on January 15.
- Top administration and ruling party officials declare intentions of legal action against what official calls "illegal" intervention by foreign labour leaders in the ongoing national strikes.

- As the already suffering South Korean economy is swept up in the recent hurricane of national strikes, nearly 1,000 small and medium businesses are beginning to face management crises due to stoppages in the car manufacturing sector.
